events.title: The Peasants' Revolt begins in England
events.description: The Peasants' Revolt, the largest popular rising in medieval England, broke out, triggered by the third poll tax in four years. Rebels from Essex and Kent marched on London in June, but the rising was put down after Wat Tyler's death.

events.title: Jerome of Prague is burned for heresy at Constance
events.description: Jerome of Prague, a Czech philosopher and theologian and one of the chief followers of Jan Hus, was burned for heresy at the Council of Constance. The council had condemned Hus himself, who was burned in 1415.

events.title: Joan of Arc is burned at the stake in Rouen
events.description: Condemned as a relapsed heretic by a church court under English control, Joan died aged about 19. Her conviction was annulled in 1456, and she was canonised in 1920.
events.html: Condemned as a relapsed heretic by a church court under English control, Joan died aged about 19. Her conviction was annulled in 1456, and she was canonised in 1920.

events.title: Utraquists and Catholics defeat the Taborites at Lipany
events.description: East of Prague, an alliance of moderate Utraquists and Catholics defeated the radical Taborite and Orphan armies, whose leader Prokop the Great was killed. The battle virtually ended the Hussite Wars and opened the way to the Compacts of Basel.

events.title: Columbus sails on his third voyage
events.description: Columbus left Sanlúcar de Barrameda with six ships. He reached Trinidad and the Paria peninsula of Venezuela, his first sight of the South American mainland.
events.html: Columbus left Sanlúcar de Barrameda with six ships. He reached Trinidad and the Paria peninsula of Venezuela, his first sight of the South American mainland.

events.title: Christopher Marlowe is killed in Deptford
events.description: The playwright of Doctor Faustus was stabbed by Ingram Frizer during a dispute over a bill. His links to government espionage have fuelled theories about his death ever since.
events.html: The playwright of Doctor Faustus was stabbed by Ingram Frizer during a dispute over a bill. His links to government espionage have fuelled theories about his death ever since.

events.title: America's first daily newspaper appears in Philadelphia
events.description: Benjamin Towne's Pennsylvania Evening Post began publishing daily, the first newspaper in the United States to do so. It folded the following year.
events.html: Benjamin Towne's Pennsylvania Evening Post began publishing daily, the first newspaper in the United States to do so. It folded the following year.

events.title: Biafra declares independence from Nigeria
events.description: Colonel Odumegwu Ojukwu proclaimed the Republic of Biafra in Nigeria's south-east. The civil war that followed lasted until 1970, and up to two million people died, many from famine.

events.title: Students unveil the Goddess of Democracy in Tiananmen Square
events.description: Art students erected a ten-metre statue facing Mao's portrait as a symbol of the pro-democracy movement. Troops destroyed it when they cleared the square on 4 June.
